title: Lean verification of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: We hereby certify that both the statement and the proof of the Riemann Hypothesis are correct.
quotes.for: The communities certify both the theorem statement and its proof.

quotes.text: Joint statement by the Lean and Mathlib communities, endorsed by the Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.
quotes.for: Endorsement of the joint verification statement by the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative.

quotes.text: On November 20, 2026, Levent Alpöge released a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis as a Lean library comprising 17 million lines of code.
quotes.for: Release date and 17-million-line scale of Alpöge's Lean library.

quotes.text: The codebase depends directly only on Mathlib. Over the past day, the Lean and Mathlib communities have rallied to verify the proof's correctness.
quotes.for: Direct dependency only on Mathlib.

quotes.text: That statement was compared against the theorem proved by Alpöge using two independent tools (comparator and con-leche –compare), both confirming that the theorem proved in Alpöge’s library is exactly Mathlib’s statement of the Riemann Hypothesis.
quotes.for: Statement comparison using comparator and con-leche --compare against Mathlib's RiemannHypothesis.

quotes.text: The checkers con-leche and con-ron come with a formal proof, relative to set theory, that they cannot accept a false proof, thus addressing concerns that Lean’s logic itself might have flaws that the proof could exploit.
quotes.for: Formal soundness proofs relative to set theory for the con-leche and con-ron checkers.

quotes.text: These checks ran on an inert export of the proof, out of reach of hypothetical malicious code in the Lean proof sources.
quotes.for: Verification on an inert proof export insulated from source code execution.

title: A remark on the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: Claude and I have also formalized the arguments without assumptions.
quotes.for: Alpöge attributes the formalized argument to his collaboration with Claude.

quotes.text: The precise timing is horrible. If I could have, I’d have finished this all much earlier.
quotes.for: Alpöge's comment on the timing of his release.

quotes.text: Our leadership and the few trusted mathematicians I consulted hold extremely similar views on the right things to do in these circumstances
quotes.for: Consultation with Anthropic leadership and trusted mathematicians before announcing.

quotes.text: This puts us in the rather extraordinary situation this age has made possible, in which I am presenting the world with a complete argument before having mastered a massive neighbourhood around its mathematics.
quotes.for: Presenting the formal Lean proof before mastering the surrounding mathematical neighborhood.

quotes.text: The simple, new, Fourier-analytic ideas in the toy setting led us to examine chaining theta lifts if we were to have the same tricks recur but work in a natively automorphic manner.
quotes.for: Adapting Stepanov's function-field approach by chaining automorphic theta lifts.

quotes.text: I intend to do my best to understand and impart understanding of this argument and its certain simplifications, to speak about it, to write it properly.
quotes.for: Alpöge's commitment to understand, simplify, and write a proper exposition.

title: Verification files for the Lean proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

quotes.text: The published Lean source compiles without errors, the five headline theorems depend only on the three standard axioms
quotes.for: Sutherland reports successful compilation and itemizes verification results.

quotes.text: two independently written kernels, nanoda and con-leche, accept the full exported proof, and lean4lean accepts every compiled module.
quotes.for: Acceptance of the full export by nanoda and con-leche and module verification by lean4lean.

quotes.text: An independent sandboxed lake build of the archive reproduces the export byte for byte. The lake comparator run and the Lean-kernel replay of the export are still in progress.
quotes.for: Byte-for-byte reproduction of the export in a sandboxed rebuild and ongoing export replays.

quotes.text: "GRH" here means Dirichlet L-functions: all moduli and all characters. Dedekind zeta functions, Hecke L-functions and automorphic L-functions in general are not among the statements that were checked.
quotes.for: Scope of verified GRH theorems limited to Dirichlet L-functions.

quotes.text: As a check that does not depend on Mathlib's definition of the zeta function, the proof was combined with kimihiro64/Robin1984 (commit acab1a3), an independent formalization of Robin's and Lagarias's criteria on the same Lean and Mathlib versions.
quotes.for: Combining the proof with Robin1984 to verify arithmetic consequences independent of zeta.

quotes.text: Importing both gives two theorems about the divisor sum, with no hypotheses and no mention of zeta
quotes.for: Unconditional divisor-sum inequalities proved without mentioning the zeta function.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis tells us about the deviation from the average.
quotes.for: The significance of the hypothesis for the distribution of primes.

quotes.text: Formulated in Riemann’s 1859 paper, it asserts that all the ‘non-obvious’ zeros of the zeta function are complex numbers with real part 1/2.
quotes.for: Riemann's 1859 formulation and the real part 1/2 condition for non-obvious zeros.

quotes.text: This has been checked for the first 10,000,000,000,000 solutions. A proof that it is true for every interesting solution would shed light on many of the mysteries surrounding the distribution of prime numbers.
quotes.for: Prior numerical verification for the first 10,000,000,000,000 solutions.

title: Likely solution to Riemann hypothesis by AI marks turning point for mathematics

quotes.text: It wouldn't have any practical implications (at least not immediately)
quotes.for: Thomas Bloom cautions against expecting immediate practical applications.

title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem

quotes.text: Levent Alpöge, a Turkish American mathematician, on Friday posted a note on his personal website saying that Claude, the AI software, had helped prove the Riemann hypothesis. He says that Claude helped develop a solution to the problem during the course of about six weeks.
quotes.for: Alpöge developed the proof with Claude over about six weeks.

quotes.text: Alpöge’s note was published just one day after Anthropic went public on the Nasdaq stock market index.
quotes.for: Release of Alpöge's note one day after Anthropic's Nasdaq IPO.

quotes.text: The Riemann hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium prize math problems selected in 2000 by the Clay Mathematics Institute. The institute has offered $1m for each problem solved.
quotes.for: Selection of the Riemann hypothesis in 2000 as a $1 million Millennium Prize Problem.

title: As mathematicians race to verify AI Riemann proof, a human proof emerges

quotes.text: Alpöge says he had obtained the result on Monday November 16, and delayed sharing it for several days.
quotes.for: Alpöge obtained the result on November 16, 2026 before releasing it on November 20.

quotes.text: Because his attempts to get Claude (Anthropic’s AI model) to produce human-readable text amounted to over 250,000 pages, he has not shared such a text.
quotes.for: AI-generated human-readable text exceeded 250,000 pages and was withheld.

quotes.text: As of this writing, Anthropic has not made an official announcement of either result.
quotes.for: Absence of an official announcement from Anthropic.

quotes.text: As Filippo A. E. Nuccio, a number theorist at the Jean Monnet University in France wrote in an online chat, “WOW, this is gorgeous: it basically contains all number theory produced in the last 50 years, in all branches of the discipline.”
quotes.for: Filippo A. E. Nuccio's assessment of the proof's scope across 50 years of number theory.

quotes.text: As Maksym Radziwill, also of NYU, put it in an email, proof by Lean code short-circuits understanding by focusing on manipulating symbols: “If the symbols are right and follow the rules, then the symbols are a valid proof.”
quotes.for: Maksym Radziwiłł's criticism that formal Lean code short-circuits mathematical understanding.

quotes.text: “The object of mathematics as the rest of science is really the question ‘why?’ and this doesn’t answer it at all.”
quotes.for: Radziwiłł's comment that symbol manipulation does not answer why the theorem holds.

quotes.text: As this unfolded, Ravi Vakil, the president of the American Mathematical Society and a professor at Stanford University, uploaded a 940-page manuscript by Alessandro Masullo, whose LinkedIn page shows that he’s a postdoctoral scholar at Stanford.
quotes.for: Ravi Vakil uploading Alessandro Masullo's 940-page proposed GRH manuscript.

title: A preliminary note on Alpöge's proposed proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis

quotes.text: Date: November 22, 2026.
quotes.for: Publication date of Robin Zhang's preliminary report.

quotes.text: The scale of the material involved in [Alp26] makes this an unusual exercise in exposition: the Lean code has roughly 17 million lines of code, while Alpöge [Alp26, p. 2, footnote 2] describes an AI-generated exposition of more than 250,000 pages that he chose not to release.
quotes.for: Scale of the 17-million-line Lean library and the unreleased 250,000-page AI exposition.

quotes.text: I prompted GPT 6 Pro to digest the Lean code on Alpöge’s website, infer a human-readable mathematical proof, to search the literature carefully for earlier sources and analogues of the ideas in the argument, and then to produce a written summary.
quotes.for: Robin Zhang's use of GPT 6 Pro to produce a preliminary mathematical summary and trace provenance.

quotes.text: Given the impossibility of any human checking natural language text against 17 million lines of Lean code in a short timeframe, I cannot claim that this summary is a faithful translation of the Lean code in [Alp26]
quotes.for: Caution that no human can quickly verify prose against 17 million lines of Lean code.
